title: Operator Assist: Runtime + Observability Integration Roadmap
author: Sofia Martinez
content:
Summary:
This roadmap describes the multi-quarter plan to integrate Operator Assist (our operator-facing automation and decision-support agent) tightly with the runtime and observability surfaces. Deliverables cover: an Operator SDK for on-call and operator UIs, a canonical telemetry contract, dashboard templates, alert-to-playbook wiring, automated remediation hooks, and a staged rollout to production operator pools. The goal is to reduce manual intervention time by 40% and mean time to mitigation (MTTM) for token-latency incidents by 30% within the first 6 months after GA.

Background and motivation:
- Problem: Operators spend significant effort context switching across siloed dashboards (runtime, traces, billing) and executing manual remediation steps during LLM inference degradation events.
- Opportunity: We can reduce cognitive load by providing curated, action-oriented operator surfaces that combine runtime signals, model-variant state, and tenant cost impacts into single decision cards.
- Scope: Runtime (inference-router, batcher, kvcache-shard-manager), Observability (token-latency SLI, prefix-cache hit-rate, model-variant error-rate), Operator Assist agent, and Operator Console UI.

Goals & success metrics (SMART):
1) Operator efficiency: 40% reduction in average hands-on time per incident (measured via operator-time logs).
2) MTTM: 30% reduction for Tier-1 token-latency incidents (baseline Q3 2027).
3) Automation coverage: 60% of high-confidence remediation actions automated behind an opt-in rollout.
4) Telemetry completeness: 100% of operator decision cards must reference at least three independent signals (runtime latency, SLO burn, cost delta).
5) Safety: No more than 1% false-positive automated remediation activations in canary cohort.

High-level milestones and timeline:
- Q4 2027: Telemetry contract v0.1, prototype decision-card UI, pilot with two operator pods.
- Q1 2028: Operator SDK alpha (Python + TS), dashboard templates (Grafana/Looker), alert-to-playbook mapping DSL v0.3.
- Q2 2028: Automated remediation operator hooks (dry-run), expanded pilot (5 pods), SLI/alert refinement.
- Q3 2028: Canary rollout of opt-in automated remediation to 20% production traffic, full runbook integration.
- Q4 2028: GA; organizational enablement, training curriculum, and SLA-backed automation SLAs.

Deliverables (per milestone):
- Telemetry contract v0.1: JSON schema for operator decision cards (fields: service, model_variant, region, slo_window_5m, slo_burn_pct, median_token_latency_ms, p95_token_latency_ms, prefix_cache_hit_pct, tenant_id_impact_estimate_usd).
- Operator SDK (alpha):
  - python package: redwood_operator_sdk (pip install redwood-operator-sdk==0.1.0a) with helpers: fetch_decision_card(), runbook_inject(), remediation_simulate().
  - ts package: @redwood/operator-sdk (npm i @redwood/operator-sdk@0.1.0-alpha).
- Dashboard templates: Grafana JSON for: OperatorDecisionCardOverview, CrossRegionTokenLatencyHeatmap, RemediationSafetyMonitor.
- Alert-to-playbook DSL: small declarative language to map signal predicates to runbook steps and opt-in automation policies.
- Playbook library: curated runbooks (token-latency, kv-cache-thrash, model-variant-fallback, burst-eviction) with explicit preconditions and rollback steps.

Ownership and operating model:
- Product owner: Priya Desai (Platform Observability).
- Technical lead: Marcus Lee (Runtime & Serving).
- Operator tooling lead: Liam O'Connor (Operator Experience).
- Cross-functional contributors: eng-sre (alerting), eng-platform (dashboards), eng-serving-runtime (telemetry), applied-ml (model-variant safety).
- Weekly cadence: roadmap sync (Wed 10:30), canary review (bi-weekly), telemetry contract review (monthly).

Concrete SLOs, SLAs and alert thresholds (examples):
- Token latency SLO (tenant-facing): 95th percentile token latency <= 350ms over 5-minute sliding window. Alert when p95 > 400ms for 3 consecutive 1-minute buckets. Severity: P1.
- Model-variant error-rate: 1-minute error-rate > 0.5% -> P2 alert.
- Prefix cache hit-rate: drop below 65% for 10 minutes -> P2.
- Cost delta guardrail: automated remediation not allowed if estimated tenant cost delta > $50/hour unless approved by owner.

Dashboards and alerting integration pattern:
1) OperatorDecisionCardOverview (single pane) shows: top 5 active decision cards, each card includes key signals, suggested remediation, confidence, and estimated cost impact.
2) Decision card expands to show trace links (OpenTelemetry span ids), last successful remediation, and quick actions (annotate, escalate, run remediation, simulate).
3) Alerts map to decision cards using the telemetry contract: an alert creates or updates a decision card with UID = alert.id + service + region.
4) Alert enrichment pipeline: alerts -> alert-enricher service (adds model variant & tenant scoring) -> operator-assist -> operator-console.

Runbook wiring examples (numbered steps):
1) Token-latency P1 decision card generated: operator-assist populates card with p95=620ms, SLO burn=38%, prefix_cache_hit=42% and tenant_cost_delta=$12/hr.
2) Suggested playbook: runbook: token-latency-fast-path-v2
   - Step 1 (read-only): collect last 100 traces: `rw-cli traces query --service inference-router --filter \"tenant_id=xyz\" --limit 100`
   - Step 2 (non-destructive): toggle prefetch hint to cohort fallback: `rw-cli operator sdk prefetch set-cohort --cohort-id=low-prefix-30m --mode=defer --dry-run`
   - Step 3 (safe write): if step 2 reduces p95 by >= 15% in dry-run experiment, execute automated remediation (opt-in).
   - Rollback: operator-assist will automatically reverse prefetch changes if p95 increases > 5% within 10 minutes.

Automated remediation safety and guardrails:
- All automation runs in two phases: simulate (dry-run, no side effects) and execute (idempotent, guarded).
- Canary policy: only pods in canary cohort (label: operator-assist/canary=true) receive execute commands.
- Approval flow: exec action requires one of: operator approval, cross-team scheduled window, or approved quick policy for low-risk actions.
- Telemetry-based abort: automation must watch three signals (p95, error-rate, eviction-rate). If any secondary signal worsens by > 10% relative, automation aborts and rolls back.

Dependencies & risks:
- Dependency: runtime must emit prefix_cache_hit_pct and model_variant ids in alert payloads (work item: runtime telemetry PR #1893).
- Risk: Over-automation causing oscillations. Mitigation: phased opt-in, simulation-first, and automated rollback with canary cohorts.
- Dependency: Grafana/Looker templating updates require infra change window (ticket INF-2211).
- Risk: Tenant cost estimation in decision card is approximate. Mitigation: conservative thresholds and cost delta guardrails.

Operator training, runbook and playbook hygiene:
- Training modules: 3 x 90-minute labs + certification quiz for operators.
- Playbook review cadence: quarterly. Playbooks must include: owner, last_verified_date, preconditions, safe-rollback steps, observability checkpoints (what to look for).
- Playbook format: markdown-runbook with metadata header (owner, impact_rating, automation_allowed: true/false). Example header: `--- owner: \"team/platform-ops\" automation_allowed: true impact_rating: medium last_verified: 2028-02-01 ---`

Migration & rollout checklist (pre-canary):
- [ ] Telemetry contract v0.1 validated against 3 production services.
- [ ] Operator SDK alpha installed and smoke-tested in staging.
- [ ] Dashboard templates deployed to Grafana staging.
- [ ] 2 operator pods enrolled in canary; runbook dry-runs executed.
- [ ] Automation safety tests (10 synthetic scenarios) passed.
- [ ] Compliance review for any automated tenant-impacting actions.

Pilot retrospective notes (learned from Q3 pilot):
- What worked: decision cards reduced discovery time by ~25% (pilot measurement), and SDK helpers made runbook calls reproducible.
- Pain points: initial telemetry payloads lacked model_variant ids and tenant tags; fixing this reduced false positives by ~60%.
- Actions: add telemetry contract enforcement (schema checks at ingestion) and require tenant-impact_estimate_usd in all decision cards.

Appendix A — Example telemetry contract (human readable table):
- Field | Type | Example | Required
- service | string | inference-router | yes
- region | string | us-west-2 | yes
- model_variant | string | redwood-gptq-2.1b-q4 | yes
- p95_token_latency_ms | number | 620 | yes
- prefix_cache_hit_pct | number | 42 | yes
- slo_burn_pct | number | 38 | yes
- tenant_id_impact_estimate_usd | number | 12.50 | conditional (required for tenant-scoped alerts)

Appendix B — CLI snippets and examples:
- Fetch decision cards for service: `rw-cli operator list-decision-cards --service inference-router --since 2028-02-01`
- Simulate remediation: `rw-cli operator simulate-remediation --card-id dc_20280203_01 --playbook token-latency-fast-path-v2`
- Execute remediation (canary cohort only): `rw-cli operator execute-remediation --card-id dc_20280203_01 --playbook token-latency-fast-path-v2 --approve --cohort canary`

Open questions for roadmap review (to resolve in Feb 2028 design sprint):
1) Do we standardize decision-card UIDs across alerting systems (PagerDuty, internal alert bus, CloudWatch)? Proposal: normalize to `redwood:dc:{service}:{region}:{alert_id}`.
2) Should cost delta estimation be performed at alert-enricher or downstream in operator-assist? Tradeoffs: early enrichment reduces downstream work; downstream allows model-specific cost heuristics.
3) What are conservative default thresholds for automation (percent improvements required in dry-run to trigger execute)? Proposal: >= 12% p95 reduction AND no secondary-signal regressions.
